title: FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) - Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for Satellite L-Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Mei-Ling Chen

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) filter targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for Satellite L-Band Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 3132.2 MHz and bandwidth of 33.3 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Satellite L-Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator)
- Frequency Band: Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD)
- Application: Satellite L-Band Filter
- Substrate: AlN on Si
- Package: LGA (Land Grid Array)
- Design Tool: CST Studio Suite 2024
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) design targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3132.2 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       33.3 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 16.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 50.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 16.0 dB
Q Factor:               6972
Temperature Coefficient:-12.0 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.5 x 1.5 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   7
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open CST Studio Suite 2024 and load the FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3132.2 MHz, BW 33.3 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (LGA (Land Grid Array)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, AlN on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 9397 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 16.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 50 MHz offset >= 50.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 5 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 4.7 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +33 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 95%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-01-28
Devices Tested:         76
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.24 dB
Return Loss (meas):     18.3 dB
Rejection (meas):       53.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       21.1 dB
Q Factor (meas):        6972
Group Delay Variation:  5.8 ns
Power Handling:         +35 dBm
Die Yield:              93.4%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The FBAR (Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator) design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Group delay flatness improved compared to previous revision.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
